  "question": "What has been proposed to reduce the risk of an image classifier being tricked into a wrong label by small, deliberately chosen changes to its input, and by what mechanism?",
  "reference_answer": "Curvature Regularization (CURE) is proposed as a fine-tuning intervention. It adds a penalty to the ordinary training loss for changes in the input gradient between a data point and a nearby point. To target curvature efficiently, the nearby point is chosen along a gradient-derived direction, since gradients tend to align with high-curvature directions. Minimizing this penalty reduces curvature and makes the loss more locally linear. Under a local quadratic approximation, with the original loss and gradient held fixed, lower curvature increases the bounds on the smallest input change needed to cross the misclassification threshold. This makes small malicious input changes less able to cause an incorrect prediction. Experiments report robustness comparable to adversarial training, rather than a guarantee against every attack.",
  "spans": [
    "To validate our analysis, we proposed a new regularizer (CURE), which directly encourages small curvatures (in other words, promotes local linearity). This regularizer is shown to significantly improve the robustness of deep networks and even achieve performance that is comparable to adversarial training.",
